record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: How should shortcomings of classical structural-balance measures be corrected when using signed triads to quantify the robustness of a social organization? The question should account for overlapping triads, weighted signed relations, and differing agent importance or social impact within each triad.

evidence.quote: This approach has several shortcomings. First, triads are evaluated independently, i.e., the fact that each agent is likely part of diﬀerent triads at the same time is ignored. Secondly, the diﬀerent weights of each signed relation, ωij, are not taken into account. Thirdly, the importance ri of the agents composing the triad is ignored.
Correcting for these shortcomings is an open discussion.

As a possible alternative we have proposed a new weighted balance measure Tijk that takes into account not only the signs and the weights of the signed relations, but also the impact of the agents involved in the triad.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (e.g., enhancements of structural balance theory in Frontiers in Human Dynamics 2022, multilevel evaluation in Scientific Reports 2020, transitivity-based measures on arXiv:2006.02565 and arXiv:2405.02798, and weight-evolution models in MDPI 2022) propose various weighted, directed, and multilevel balance measures, but none establishes a single canonical correction that jointly handles overlapping triads, weighted ties, and heterogeneous agent importance. The problem of properly correcting classical balance under these three shortcomings remains an active open discussion.

status_evidence.title: Enhancing structural balance theory and measurement
status_evidence.snippet: Develops enhanced balance measures for signed digraphs but does not unify weights and agent importance with overlap.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on improved balance measures, indicating no settled canonical answer.

status_evidence.title: Structural balance in signed digraphs (arXiv:2006.02565)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes transitivity-based balance measures for different link signing methods.
status_evidence.claim: Continued proposals of new balance measures show problem remains under discussion.

status_evidence.title: Multilevel structural evaluation of signed directed social networks
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces multilevel balance measures across triads, subgroups, and full network.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing frameworks exist; no consensus correction.

status_evidence.title: Structural Balance in Real-World Social Networks (arXiv:2405.02798)
status_evidence.snippet: Incorporates direction and transitivity in measuring partial balance.
status_evidence.claim: Recent 2024 work still proposing refinements, suggesting the question is open.
